common_name: Lady Darlene Dahlia (Giant Red-and-Gold Bicolor Dinnerplate Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost; stake at planting time to support the heavy blooms.

directions: Lady Darlene produces huge, informal decorative blooms with rich red petals broadly tipped and splashed in golden yellow, a bold bicolor pattern that holds up well in the garden and in bouquets. Stake stems early since the dinnerplate-sized flowers are heavy enough to bend or snap unsupported canes. Disbud lateral buds to concentrate growth into fewer, larger show-quality blooms, or leave them for a bushier plant with more numerous mid-size flowers. Lift and store tubers after fall frost blackens the foliage in regions colder than zone 8.

common_name: Bednall Beauty Dahlia (Scarlet Single Dahlia with Dark Bronze Foliage)

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep after danger of frost has passed; compact habit suits containers and front-of-border placement.

directions: Bednall Beauty is a compact, old English bedding dahlia prized for the contrast between its near-black bronze foliage and its vivid single scarlet-red flowers. Its low, bushy habit makes it well suited to container growing and mixed border edging where the dark leaves provide season-long color even between flushes of bloom. Deadhead regularly to keep new buds forming, and pinch young plants once to encourage a bushier, more floriferous shape. In zones colder than 8, lift tubers after frost blackens the foliage and store them in a cool, dry, frost-free place over winter.

common_name: Preston Park Dahlia (Dwarf Scarlet Single Bedding Dahlia with Bronze Foliage)

planting.note: Set out transplants or small tubers after last frost; very compact and floriferous, ideal for edging and mass bedding.

directions: Preston Park is a dwarf bedding dahlia bred for uniform, compact mounds covered in small single scarlet-red flowers set against dark bronze-purple foliage. Its short stature and extremely free-flowering habit make it a popular choice for formal bedding schemes, edging, and containers rather than cutting. Deadhead spent flowers to keep the display tidy and encourage continuous bloom through summer and into fall. Where winters drop below zone 8, lift tubers after frost or simply treat plants as annuals and replace them the following spring.

common_name: Easter Sunday Dahlia (White Collarette Dahlia with Pale Yellow Collar)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost in well-drained soil.

directions: Easter Sunday carries the open, single-rowed outer petals typical of collarette dahlias, in crisp white, surrounding a small inner collar of pale yellow petaloids around a golden central disc. The airy, two-tiered flower form reads lighter in the garden and in arrangements than fully double dahlia types. Deadhead consistently through the season to keep plants blooming, and stake taller stems in exposed sites. Lift and store tubers over winter where temperatures fall below zone 8.

common_name: Night Butterfly Dahlia (Dark Maroon-Red Collarette with White Collar)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; benefits from staking as plants gain height.

directions: Night Butterfly pairs a single outer row of dark maroon-red petals with a contrasting inner collar of white petaloids, giving the bloom strong contrast at a distance and in bouquets. Like other collarette types, flowers are produced prolifically through summer and are lighter and more open than fully double decorative or ball forms. Deadhead regularly to sustain bloom production and stake stems in windy or exposed locations. In climates colder than zone 8, lift and store tubers after frost kills back the foliage.

common_name: Rip Van Winkle Dahlia (Shaggy Lavender-Pink Cactus Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; stake at planting time to support tall stems.

directions: Rip Van Winkle is an old cactus-flowered cultivar known for its shaggy, fully double lavender-pink blooms made up of narrow, rolled, curling petals that give the flower a loose, tousled texture distinct from stiffer-petaled cactus forms. Its long-lasting flowers and old-fashioned charm have kept it in circulation among heirloom dahlia collectors for decades. Stake plants early since mature stems can reach several feet and bend under the weight of flowers in wind or rain. Lift and store tubers after frost in regions colder than zone 8.

common_name: Prince Noir Dahlia (Deep Maroon-Black Decorative Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; stake at planting time.

directions: Prince Noir produces fully double decorative blooms in a deep, velvety maroon so dark it reads as near-black in most light, a dramatic foil for paler companions in borders and cutting beds. The broad, slightly twisted petals give the flower good substance and vase life once cut. Disbud side shoots for larger show-type blooms, or leave them for a bushier plant with more flowers of moderate size. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Jowey Mirella Dahlia (Soft Pink Ball Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost.

directions: Jowey Mirella belongs to the Jowey series of Dutch-bred ball dahlias and bears densely packed, perfectly spherical blooms in soft pink with tightly involuted petals, a hallmark of the ball class. Its tidy, uniform flower shape and sturdy stems make it a dependable cut flower as well as a reliable garden and show plant. Deadhead regularly to encourage continued bud set through the season. In regions colder than zone 8, lift and store tubers after fall frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Yellow Hammer Dahlia (Historic Dwarf Single Golden-Yellow Dahlia)

planting.note: Can also be started from seed indoors several weeks before last frost; set transplants or tubers out once frost danger has passed.

directions: Yellow Hammer is a long-grown dwarf single dahlia strain valued for its bright golden-yellow flowers held just above bronze-tinted foliage on a short, bushy plant. Its small stature and free-flowering nature have kept it popular for edging, bedding, and containers since early in the twentieth century. Deadhead spent flowers to keep plants tidy and flowering steadily through the season. Treat as an annual in cold climates or lift and store tubers over winter in zones below 8.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost.

directions: Hallmark is a classic pompon dahlia producing small, perfectly round, fully double flowers in soft lavender-pink with tightly rolled petals packed into a dense, honeycomb pattern typical of the pompon class. Its diminutive flower size and neat habit make it well suited to cutting and small arrangements rather than large garden display. Deadhead often to keep the compact plant flowering steadily through the season. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.
